findings.message: Outcome guarantee or absolute claim; not allowed in dental advertising.

findings.quote: we promise a visibly brighter smile after a single visit
findings.why: A guaranteed visible result after one visit is a promise of outcome that the ADA advertising rules prohibit, and the post itself says results vary from person to person.
findings.fix: Delete the promise and state that results vary and that the dentist will assess at the exam whether whitening is a good fit.

findings.quote: Whitening is one of the most requested cosmetic treatments, and one of the most misunderstood.
findings.why: The claim that whitening is among the most requested cosmetic treatments has no source and cannot be verified from the ficha or the links provided.
findings.fix: Remove the ranking claim or support it with a cited survey, or rephrase as a general observation without a superlative.

findings.quote: The ADA's [MouthHealthy page on teeth whitening](https://www.mouthhealthy.org/all-topics-a-z/tooth-whitening-safety) covers the basics.
findings.why: The ADA MouthHealthy domain is real, but I cannot confirm that this specific page path exists, so the link is unverified.
findings.fix: Open the URL to confirm it resolves to the ADA page on whitening safety, and replace it with the verified address if it does not.

findings.quote: The details matter, though, so here is what to know before you start.
findings.why: The generic framing sentence reads like stock AI phrasing rather than the clinic's own voice.
findings.fix: Replace it with a specific sentence about the safety points the post covers.
